Ben / Marissa —

Draft threat-summary and key technical points below. I'll attach a compact XLSX threat matrix after you review. High-level guidance we should include to reassure auditors:

1) Segmentation / Topology
- Tenants run in isolated runtime enclaves (logical tenant namespace + memory/KV isolation). No tenant topology has direct L2/L3 reachability to other tenants; we enforce inter-tenant restrictions at the flow/ACL layer at the sidecar and at the host network.
- Control plane components (scheduler, model registry, control APIs) are on a separate control network with mTLS mutual auth to all managed dataplane components. Operator consoles are isolated to a dedicated operator network behind enforced jump hosts (bastion + MFA).

2) Sidecar & Proxy model
- Every inference pod (or VM instance in dedicated deployments) runs a lightweight sidecar that performs: TLS termination to the model backend, inbound request validation, per-tenant RBAC checks, and fine-grained egress filtering.
- Sidecars embed a policy engine (Whitelists/deny-by-default) and drop any cross-tenant traffic not expressively permitted. Sidecar configs are versioned and signed; rollout uses canary with automatic rollback on policy violations.

3) KV cache & state isolation
- KV caches are namespaced by tenant with strict access controls. We use per-tenant encryption keys (wrapped by HSM/KMS) so a compromised host cannot trivially decrypt another tenant's cache. Cache access is mediated by sidecars and enforcement lives in the runtime layer.

4) Attack scenarios we model (short form)
- Sidecar compromise: mitigations = signed configs, runtime sandboxing, micro-VM boundaries for higher-assurance deployments, behavior-based telemetry (abnormal ACL churn), automatic circuit breakers.
- Lateral move via operator plane: mitigations = operator console MFA, just-in-time admin sessions, recorded sessions, and HSM-backed signing of sensitive operations.
- KV cache theft: mitigations = tenant key separation, per-token short TTL, and encrypted at-rest with periodic key rotation.

5) Detection & telemetry
- Network flows are logged at the edge and aggregated to our control-plane telemetry (immutable, append-only stream). We provide flow-level evidence for audits (pcap-lite artifacts, flow logs) and maintain 90 days by default (extendable).

6) Fail-open / fail-closed considerations
- Default is fail-closed for sidecars: policy evaluation failures result in request rejection. Critical control-plane failover has a separate, hardened path that does not increase cross-tenant access.

I will prepare a 1-page threat-likelihood table mapping probability x impact for the examples above and include recommended mitigations and evidence artifacts.

—Priyom
